item.title: Seiryuji Temple & Its Giant Daibutsu — Guide
item.description: Seiryuji sits on the wooded slopes of western Hiroshima, well away from the tourist trail, and its landmark is a huge bronze Daibutsu, a Great Buddha seated serenely on the hillside and gazing out over the city and the delta below. The temple grounds climb the slope through halls, statuary and quiet corners, with views that open up as you ascend, and the whole place sees a fraction of the visitors of the central sights.

item.title: Todaiji and the Great Buddha: Nara's Colossal Temple — Guide
item.description: Todaiji is the grandest of Nara’s temples and one of Japan’s most awe-inspiring sights: founded in 752 as the head of all provincial Buddhist temples, it houses the Daibutsu, a 15-metre seated bronze Great Buddha, one of the largest bronze statues in the world, enshrined within the Daibutsuden — for centuries the largest wooden building on earth. The approach passes through the towering Nandaimon gate, guarded by a pair of ferocious 8-metre Nio guardian statues carved in the 13th century, while sacred deer roam the grounds.
